# Flower Duet

Flower Duet

## _location\_on_ Los Angeles

## _local\_activity_ Classes and experiences: Flower Arrangement • Flower Wreath • Floristry • Terrarium • Music

5.0 (15)![Image 62: Instagram followers](https://classbento.com/images/icons/ui/instagram.svg) 3k followers

_female_ Women-owned 

  

  
 The Coleman sisters, Casey Schwartz and Kit Wertz, began their floral design business in 1999.We started Flower Duet as a part-time weekend business after Casey had finished a career as an officer on board a luxury cruise ship with ports in the Mediterranean and the Caribbean. One of her early jobs on board included designing flowers from around the world. Once Casey settled down in Los Angeles, Kit had immersed herself in floral design courses for a few years, and we started offering flower arranging parties at people's homes. Those parties led to clients who wanted to hire Flower Duet for their weddings, and a new hybrid business was born. We love creating custom wedding flowers, directing corporate team-building reward events for companies like BMW, Mattel, Universal Studios, the NFL, and Fabletics, and teaching flower arranging to budding floral designers and dedicated floral enthusiasts.Flower Duet has been our full-time passion for the last decade. It shows that we are the preferred floral vendors for many area venues, including many numerous luxury venues throughout Los Angeles.In addition to teaching flower arranging classes at our own design studio in the South Bay of Los Angeles, we also teach floral design workshops at The Huntington Library in San Marino and offer tours of the Los Angeles Floral District.Flower Duet is a proud member of the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and of Slow Flowers.Flower Duet has won two awards from the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and been the guest designer for the American Grown Flowers Field to Vase Dinner, Speakers at The Slow Flower Summit in Washington, D.C., presenters at the San Francisco Flower and Garden Show and keynote speakers for dozens of garden clubs around the Southern California area.

# About FlowerSchool

FlowerSchool was established in 2003 has locations in New York City and Los Angeles California

Flower School Los Angeles brings the most sought-after designers from all over the world to teach our uniquely comprehensive programs. Students learn everything from how to care for flowers to bouquets to large-scale floral installations and event planning.

​

Flower School Los Angeles is owned and operated by Executive Director, Caitlin Hamilton.

​

Located in the heart of Los Angeles, Flower School Los Angeles is one of the most celebrated floral design schools in the world. Flower School is the place to begin your floral education and exploration into the world of contemporary floral arranging. Flower School Los Angeles offers recreational flower arranging workshops, private events, travel programs, and more.

## Meet The Team

### Calvert Crary

Executive Director

Calvert Crary is the Executive Director of both FlowerSchool New York and FlowerSchool Los Angeles, and author of Flower School: A Practical Guide to the Art of Flower Arranging (Nov 2020).

​

An internationally recognized instructor and mentor, Calvert has taught programs across the United States, Holland, Mexico and Australia, and was this year’s judge for the prestigious PHS Philadelphia Flower Show.

​

Calvert has trained and coached thousands of students on how to work in the floral industry with top designers, start new businesses, or reorganize existing floral businesses into thriving careers.

# Flower School Los Angeles 4-Week Floral Design Program

The Floral Design Program is comprised of multiple modules that focus on critical floral design skills. The curriculum is outlined below, with approximations of the hours required to complete each series. From this specific curriculum, students not only learn the correct skills, but also build confidence in their abilities to find success in the industry.​

UPCOMING SESSIONS:  
[SEPTEMBER 2026](https://www.flowerschoolla.com/event-details-registration/4-week-floral-design-training-program-september-2026)

[JANUARY 2027](https://www.flowerschoolla.com/event-details-registration/4-week-floral-design-training-program-january-2027)

This 4 week program is the most comprehensive, hands on, floristry and design program available .

![Image 3](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/685774_17c772c25a034015895e707eab5d64c7~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_1103,h_520,fp_0.68_0.19,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/_m4a3263.jpg)

## Floral Design Program by the numbers

![Image 4: IMG_8780.JPG](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/685774_af176f930ee441628ef1f7d56a68e7b0~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_209,h_209,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/IMG_8780_JPG.jpg)

Module 01 - 10 Hours

### 2-Day Introduction to Design Series

This series of 4 classes over 2 days starts at the very beginning of floral design and teaches the elemental technical skills in floral design.

![Image 5: _m4a1777.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/685774_dc7aabd2caef4100b23a69c32a1ee736~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_209,h_209,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/_m4a1777.jpg)

Module 02 - 15 Hours

### 3-Day Intermediate Design Series

After learning the basic floristry techniques in the Introduction Series, the Intermediate Series will introduce the next level of floral design skills and techniques including purchasing flowers and building recipes.

![Image 6: _m4a9415another double page spread option.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/685774_7fae9b0f67d542cdaf0a8651b1e33db5~mv2.jpg/v1/crop/x_0,y_0,w_3000,h_3000/fill/w_209,h_209,fp_0.50_0.50,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/_m4a9415another%20double%20page%20spread%20option.jpg)

Module 03 - 6 Hours

### Introduction to Freelance &Conditioning Lab

The Conditioning Lab is a simulated design studio experience where students spend the entire day conditioning flowers for up and coming projects. There is no designing in this program, but learning to work as a freelancer.

![Image 7](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/685774_46afdc00bef14f6892ab2bf9a5b9d655~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_209,h_209,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/class%2010_1.png)

Module 04 - 10 Hours

### 2-Day Advanced Design Series

Students will learn advanced and specialized mechanics of arranging that are commonly used for achieving a specific look. Each student will also be responsible for creating a sketch of the concept and design, picking their own color palette.

![Image 8](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/685774_6442bf04d7d4491caf59866fcd61d775~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_209,h_209,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/_m4a0772.jpg)

Module 05 - 6 Hours

### Photography & Marketing

*   Marketing & Branding 101

*   Traditional vs. Content Marketing

*   How to Write a Press Release

*   Social Media Engagement, Strategic Plan & Vision

*   How to make a good photo GREAT

![Image 9: Screenshot 2024-02-15 at 2.28.30 PM.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/65379e_90f74233c81c4a7f9f77277d4e2ec23e~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_209,h_209,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Screenshot%202024-02-15%20at%202_28_30%E2%80%AFPM.png)

Module 06 - 6 Hours

### Floristry for Special Events: Wiring & Ribbons Workshop

This is the space to describe the service and explain how customers or clients can benefit from it. It’s an opportunity to add a short description that includes relevant details, like pricing, duration, location and how to book the service.

![Image 10: IMG_2970.heic](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/788747_4ea22c1046b34388a040e3fa956fd416~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_209,h_209,fp_0.38_0.39,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/IMG_2970_heic.png)

Module 07- 12 Hours

### 2-Day Large-Scale Installations

This 2-day series focuses on large scale installations for maximum wow. The installations program teaches large scale sculpture with living materials and includes an elevated centerpiece design, large-scale monumental urn, flowering arch and hanging arrangement.

![Image 11: _m4a7109.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/685774_146b84807f254e7a9a5ba47f85a0baa3~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_209,h_209,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/_m4a7109.jpg)

Module 08- 6 Hours

### Sympathy Style & Decor

Don't let this program intimidate you. Making wreaths and sprays are the signature for all florists

![Image 12: Stem&Bud_wreath-03 (1).jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/685774_2ffffb7e59824d83a3bd4bdfb44af0f1~mv2.jpg/v1/crop/x_475,y_1278,w_2896,h_2896/fill/w_209,h_209,fp_0.50_0.50,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Stem%26Bud_wreath-03%20(1).jpg)

Module 09- 5 Hours

### Decorating with Flowers

## Learn how to craft tablescapes, wreaths, garlands, and seasonal floral designs that bring creativity to holidays throughout the year and beauty into events & everyday spaces.

![Image 13: Screenshot 2025-03-13 at 12.56.43 AM.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/788747_855a1fc021fc4118ba834a704a92b530~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_209,h_209,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Screenshot%202025-03-13%20at%2012_56_43%E2%80%AFAM.png)

Module 10- 15 Hours

### 3 Day Wedding Design Series

## Learn the full process of creating the overall floral design for a wedding. Create storyboards, receive instruction in conducting consultations and making proposals, learn how to purchase floral products within your budget, and create a mock-execution of the event’s designs.

![Image 14: _m4a3256.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/685774_2cd9658ca8ac493fa2ffc2b740c279ca~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_1271,h_500,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/_m4a3256.jpg)

ENROLLMENT FORM & POLICY

​

Registration for all classes is limited to 14 students. Students are advised to register as soon as possible to ensure their enrollment in the Floral Design Program. Registrations are held once the $600 deposit fee is paid and an email confirmation is sent to [info@flowerschoolla.com](mailto:info@flowerschoolla.com) expressing your commitment and agreement to pay full course fee by start of the program. Student will be provided an enrollment agreement, which needs to be signed and returned to secure placement.

No refunds or cancellations are allowed within 7 days of the start of the course. Course dates, times, and agendas are subject to change—students with questions should check with Flower School staff.

Students must be at least 18 years of age at the start of the program.

![Image 15](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/685774_2e8b6cb9379a4f18b185b281a3730cd6~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_424,h_469,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/_calvert_crary.jpg)

## Payment & Refund Policy

PAYMENT SCHEDULE & METHODS  
  
 The FlowerSchool 4-Week Floral Design Program accepts students on a rolling registration basis. We require that each student submit their paperwork at a minimum of 7 days before the start of the program.  
  
 Interval Students  
 Students who are not able to attend the 4-weeks consecutively will be placed in our interval group. This group will be able to take modules of the program when with schedule permits. They will graduate with the next group of students graduates.  
  
 Tuition Refund & Cancellation Policy  
 A student who cancels within 7 days of signing the enrollment agreement but before instruction begins receives all monies returned with the exception of the non-refundable $600 registration deposit fee.  
  
 Thereafter, a student will be liable for:

1.   The non-refundable registration fee plus

2.   The cost of any textbooks, supplies accepted plus

3.   Registration fee liability as of the student’s last date of physical attendance. Liability is determined by the percentage of the program offered to the student.

IF TERMINATION OCCURS THE SCHOOL MAY KEEP:  
 0 – 15% of the program: 35%  
 16 – 35% of the program: 66%  
 36 – 50% of the program: 80%  
 After 51% of the program:100%  
  
 If the school cancels or discontinues its program, the school will make a full refund of all tuition paid for that period.

# Flower Arranging: Oaks and Fifth Season Florals

Event

* * *

Make a make a vibrant floral design inspired by American oak landscapes.

Participants will create a striking floral design featuring foliage, fall grasses, pods, and roses in this hands-on workshop led by [Flower Duet](https://flowerduet.com/).

## Key Details

*   Registration includes free admission to The Huntington after the program ends.
*   Suitable for all levels; no previous experience is necessary.
*   This class is open to participants ages 12 and older. Registered participants under 18 must be accompanied by an adult with a class ticket.
*   All supplies and materials are included. 
*   Please bring registration confirmation with you. 
*   The workshop will be held outdoors, so please dress comfortably.
*   Check in with Education staff at Admission window #9 at 9:30 a.m. or 12:30 p.m., depending on class time.

## In-Person Class Ticketing Policies

*   **Tickets are not sold at the door for this event.**
*   **To join the waitlist for this event, please email notify the Public Programs team.** A space is not guaranteed, but you will be contacted if a space becomes available.
*   **To receive a refund or request a reservation change, you must contact the Public Programs team at least five days prior to the event date.** Cancellations made within five days of the event date will not be refunded, and reservation changes are not guaranteed. Tickets are nontransferable and cannot be exchanged for vouchers or future credit.
*   **Members may receive a discount for up to two tickets when applicable.**

For questions about this event, please contact the Public Programs team at [publicprograms@huntington.org.](mailto:publicprograms@huntington.org)

_Program fees support our mission to promote education in the arts, humanities, and botanical sciences._

In-Person Flower Arranging Classes & Online Flower Courses[Kit Wertz](https://flowerduet.com/author/kit-wertz/)2026-05-25T14:04:19-07:00

![Image 2: flowerclass](https://flowerduet.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/flowerclass-e1779743051221.webp)

Our hands-on Flower Arrang­ing work­shops in Los Ange­les are designed to remove any intim­i­da­tion from work­ing with flow­ers and enhance your abil­i­ty to feel con­fi­dent in flo­ral design. Led by our Mas­ter Design­ers, Casey and Kit, Co-Founders and Own­ers of Flower Duet, each class and work­shop fea­tures essen­tial knowl­edge on how to choose fresh flow­ers, how to treat them with care, design mas­ter tech­niques, and always pre­mi­um sea­son­al blooms.

Open to all lev­els, our work­shops are ide­al for flower enthu­si­asts of all lev­els, from begin­ners to expe­ri­enced. Every work­shop expe­ri­ence is a per­fect out­ing for friend dates, solo soul cleans­ing, team out­ings, or try­ing out a new skill.

##### We offer flower arranging workshops at our studio and on location:

*   Sea­son­al and themed workshops
*   Pri­vate work­shops for indi­vid­u­als and groups

*   Client appre­ci­a­tion experiences
*   Book our stu­dio for pri­vate events and cel­e­bra­tions, along with a cus­tomized flower work­shop for your group. We’ve host­ed baby show­ers, bridal show­ers, birth­days, book clubs, alum­ni groups, and all types of phil­an­thropic groups for our flower classes

Florist Owner-Designing Sisters[Kit Wertz](https://flowerduet.com/author/kit-wertz/)2026-10-01T20:50:07-07:00

# Flower Duet’s Award-Winning Floral Design Team

![Image 2: Casey Schwartz and Kit Wertz from Flower Duet](https://flowerduet.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/casey_kit_flowerduet_2025-600x600.jpg)The Cole­man sis­ters, Casey Schwartz and Kit Wertz, began their flo­ral design busi­ness in 1999.

We start­ed Flower Duet as a part-time week­end busi­ness after Casey had retired from design­ing flow­ers on lux­u­ry cruise ships around the world (see Casey’s biog­ra­phy below) and Kit had immersed her­self in flo­ral design cours­es for a few years. We love cre­at­ing cus­tom wed­ding flow­ers, direct­ing cor­po­rate team-build­ing reward events for com­pa­nies like BMW, Mat­tel, Uni­ver­sal Stu­dios, the NFL, and Fablet­ics, and teach­ing flower arrang­ing to bud­ding flo­ral design­ers and ded­i­cat­ed flo­ral enthusiasts.

Flower Duet has been our full-time pas­sion for the last decade. It shows that we are the pre­ferred flo­ral ven­dors for many area venues includ­ing Ter­ranea, The Redon­do Beach His­toric Library, The Portofi­no Hotel, La Ven­ta Inn, Rolling Hills Coun­try Club, Palos Verdes Golf Club, Hotel Maya, Shade Hotel Redon­do Beach, Shade Hotel Man­hat­tan Beach,and Los Verdes Golf Course. We often cre­ate designs for pri­vate par­ties, cor­po­rate galas, and wed­dings at oth­er local area venues includ­ing The Cal­i­for­nia Surf Club, South Coast Botan­ic Gar­den, Blue­wa­ter Grill, King Har­bor Yacht Club, and The Rex Steakhouse.

In addi­tion to teach­ing **[flower arrang­ing class­es](http://flowerduet.com/workshops/ "Flower Arranging Classes Los Angeles")** at our own design stu­dio in the South Bay of Los Ange­les, we also teach flo­ral design work­shops at **[The Hunt­ing­ton Library](http://flowerduet.com/flower-arranging-classes/huntington-library/ "Huntington Library Floral Design Classes")** in San Marino.

Flower Duet is a proud mem­ber of the **[Tor­rance Area Cham­ber of Com­merce](https://www.torrancechamber.com/)**and [**Slow Flow­ers**](https://www.slowflowers.com/).

Flower Duet has won two awards from the Tor­rance Area Cham­ber of Com­merce and been the guest design­er for the Taste of LA and Amer­i­can Grown Flow­ers Field to Vase Din­ner, Speak­ers at The Slow Flower Sum­mit in Wash­ing­ton, D.C., pre­sen­ters at the San Fran­cis­co Flower and Gar­den Show and keynote speak­ers for dozens of gar­den clubs around the South­ern Cal­i­for­nia area. We’ve appeared in major news­pa­pers includ­ing [_**The New York Times**_](https://flowerduet.com/new-york-times/) and on television.

### Casey Coleman Schwartz

![Image 3: Casey Coleman Schwartz of Flower Duet](https://flowerduet.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/casey_2025-300x293.jpg)Casey was inspired by flow­ers her whole life through our par­ents’ beau­ti­ful gar­dens and love of all types of flow­ers and plants. After Casey grad­u­at­ed from Ohio Uni­ver­si­ty with a bach­e­lor’s degree in Recre­ation Man­age­ment, she achieved her goal to work on cruise ships and to chase sum­mer around the globe.

Casey start­ed her flo­ral design career on a lux­u­ry cruise ship called The Sea God­dess I, part of the leg­endary [Cunard](http://www.cunard.com/) lines. It was one of her ear­ly jobs on the ship to cre­ate and main­tain the live flo­ral designs on the ship for 7–10 days and to buy flow­ers from ven­dors at port cities around the world in mul­ti­ple lan­guages and currencies.

After act­ing as Chief Purs­er for six years on the ship and ful­fill­ing her dream of fol­low­ing sum­mer around the globe, this Cal­i­for­nia native set­tled down in Los Ange­les to be close to her broth­er and sis­ter. She con­tin­ued to take flo­ral design cours­es includ­ing com­plet­ing her advanced flo­ral design certificate.

Casey’s design aes­thet­ic knows no bounds. She is open to all flow­ers and all types of design. She can mim­ic any style and has a won­der­ful, warm invit­ing per­son­al style of her own which is evi­dent in all the rela­tion­ships she has with her clients and students.

### Kit Wertz

![Image 4: Kit Coleman Wertz of Flower Duet](https://flowerduet.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/kit_2025Headshot-285x300.jpeg)Like her sis­ter Casey, Kit had a love of flow­ers from an ear­ly age thanks to the love­ly flow­ers her moth­er grew every sum­mer in the back­yard. Dur­ing col­lege, Kit worked as a peren­ni­al plant spe­cial­ist at a local nurs­ery and after grad­u­at­ing from James Madi­son Uni­ver­si­ty with a bach­e­lor’s degree in Jour­nal­ism, Kit had the oppor­tu­ni­ty to work in The Nether­lands. Kit became pas­sion­ate about flo­ral design after liv­ing among the flower-lov­ing Dutch and after she cre­at­ed her own wed­ding flow­ers (with Casey’s help) for her wed­ding in 1997. Kit fell in love with the Los Ange­les Flo­ral Dis­trict and want­ed to share that pas­sion for flow­ers with her friends.

After tak­ing friends down to the mart and show­ing them how to cre­ate flower designs, the con­cept of Flower Duet took shape. By teach­ing peo­ple how to design flow­ers in their own homes in a flower par­ty atmos­phere, Flower Duet was able to grow through refer­rals for wed­dings and spe­cial event flowers.

Kit’s back­ground is in pho­to­jour­nal­ism, so her cre­ative eye is a plus when try­ing a new flo­ral design idea. While work­ing as an Inter­net mar­ket­ing expert for com­pa­nies like Office Depot and Toy­ota Motor Sales, U.S.A., Kit honed her flo­ral design skills by tak­ing class­es and work­shops around South­ern California.

# Viola Floral

Viola Floral

## _location\_on_ Santa Monica, Los Angeles

## _local\_activity_ Classes: Flower Arrangement • Ikebana • Flower Wreath • Floristry • Photography

![Image 62: Instagram followers](https://classbento.com/images/icons/ui/instagram.svg) 17k followers 5.0 (2)

_female_ Women-owned 

  

  
 Viola Floral was founded in 2019 by Jelena Trifunovic — floral designer, science educator, and mom of three. Jelena was born and raised in Serbia and moved to Los Angeles at the start of the Yugoslav War in the early 1990s. She studied biology and took her love of science to the classroom — first as a high school teacher and then as a professor at Loyola Marymount University.Jelena grew up arranging flowers with her mother, entertaining and hosting many gatherings both at home and at her family’s restaurant. After her mother passed away from pancreatic cancer in 2016, Jelena decided to pursue her passion for floral design by launching Viola Floral — honoring the bond the two women shared in a meaningful way. Viola Floral began as a labor of love and a path for Jelena to heal, but now (many years and tens of thousands of bouquets later), Jelena leads a team of designers who share her passion for flowers and floral education.

The Coleman sisters, Casey Schwartz and Kit Wertz, began their floral design business in 1999.We started Flower Duet as a part-time weekend business after Casey had finished a career as an officer on board a luxury cruise ship with ports in the Mediterranean and the Caribbean. One of her early jobs on board included designing flowers from around the world. Once Casey settled down in Los Angeles, Kit had immersed herself in floral design courses for a few years, and we started offering flower arranging parties at people's homes. Those parties led to clients who wanted to hire Flower Duet for their weddings, and a new hybrid business was born. We love creating custom wedding flowers, directing corporate team-building reward events for companies like BMW, Mattel, Universal Studios, the NFL, and Fabletics, and teaching flower arranging to budding floral designers and dedicated floral enthusiasts.Flower Duet has been our full-time passion for the last decade. It shows that we are the preferred floral vendors for many area venues, including many numerous luxury venues throughout Los Angeles.In addition to teaching flower arranging classes at our own design studio in the South Bay of Los Angeles, we also teach floral design workshops at The Huntington Library in San Marino and offer tours of the Los Angeles Floral District.Flower Duet is a proud member of the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and of Slow Flowers.Flower Duet has won two awards from the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and been the guest designer for the American Grown Flowers Field to Vase Dinner, Speakers at The Slow Flower Summit in Washington, D.C., presenters at the San Francisco Flower and Garden Show and keynote speakers for dozens of garden clubs around the Southern California area.

Viola Floral was founded in 2019 by Jelena Trifunovic — floral designer, science educator, and mom of three. Jelena was born and raised in Serbia and moved to Los Angeles at the start of the Yugoslav War in the early 1990s. She studied biology and took her love of science to the classroom — first as a high school teacher and then as a professor at Loyola Marymount University.Jelena grew up arranging flowers with her mother, entertaining and hosting many gatherings both at home and at her family’s restaurant. After her mother passed away from pancreatic cancer in 2016, Jelena decided to pursue her passion for floral design by launching Viola Floral — honoring the bond the two women shared in a meaningful way. Viola Floral began as a labor of love and a path for Jelena to heal, but now (many years and tens of thousands of bouquets later), Jelena leads a team of designers who share her passion for flowers and floral education.

Viola Floral was founded in 2019 by Jelena Trifunovic — floral designer, science educator, and mom of three. Jelena was born and raised in Serbia and moved to Los Angeles at the start of the Yugoslav War in the early 1990s. She studied biology and took her love of science to the classroom — first as a high school teacher and then as a professor at Loyola Marymount University.Jelena grew up arranging flowers with her mother, entertaining and hosting many gatherings both at home and at her family’s restaurant. After her mother passed away from pancreatic cancer in 2016, Jelena decided to pursue her passion for floral design by launching Viola Floral — honoring the bond the two women shared in a meaningful way. Viola Floral began as a labor of love and a path for Jelena to heal, but now (many years and tens of thousands of bouquets later), Jelena leads a team of designers who share her passion for flowers and floral education.

The Coleman sisters, Casey Schwartz and Kit Wertz, began their floral design business in 1999.We started Flower Duet as a part-time weekend business after Casey had finished a career as an officer on board a luxury cruise ship with ports in the Mediterranean and the Caribbean. One of her early jobs on board included designing flowers from around the world. Once Casey settled down in Los Angeles, Kit had immersed herself in floral design courses for a few years, and we started offering flower arranging parties at people's homes. Those parties led to clients who wanted to hire Flower Duet for their weddings, and a new hybrid business was born. We love creating custom wedding flowers, directing corporate team-building reward events for companies like BMW, Mattel, Universal Studios, the NFL, and Fabletics, and teaching flower arranging to budding floral designers and dedicated floral enthusiasts.Flower Duet has been our full-time passion for the last decade. It shows that we are the preferred floral vendors for many area venues, including many numerous luxury venues throughout Los Angeles.In addition to teaching flower arranging classes at our own design studio in the South Bay of Los Angeles, we also teach floral design workshops at The Huntington Library in San Marino and offer tours of the Los Angeles Floral District.Flower Duet is a proud member of the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and of Slow Flowers.Flower Duet has won two awards from the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and been the guest designer for the American Grown Flowers Field to Vase Dinner, Speakers at The Slow Flower Summit in Washington, D.C., presenters at the San Francisco Flower and Garden Show and keynote speakers for dozens of garden clubs around the Southern California area.

 Tour the famous Los Angeles floral district with an expert florist from LA-based FLOWER DUET! Whether you're an aspiring florist, have always been curious about the LA Flower Mart, or simply want to connect with nature, this tour is a great way to learn more about the city and craft!Choose between a private or group flower mart tour of the downtown Los Angeles Floral District — affectionately known as “the LA Flower Mart.” You'll explore the two main markets that make up the LA Floral District, which are over 100 years old: the Southern California Flower Market and The Original Los Angeles Flower Market. They make up the largest wholesale flower district in the United States and are open to the public through a joint program.Learn how to find fresh flowers and the buying etiquette, to make shopping on your own a breeze. You'll learn where to find floral supplies around the market area and the safest place to park while shopping. We offer over 20 years of experience shopping in the market, so you’ll feel confident and welcome to shop again and again.Please be on time, tours start promptly. If you are taking our class in Torrance at 10 a.m., we offer you a little time at the end to shop.

The Coleman sisters, Casey Schwartz and Kit Wertz, began their floral design business in 1999.We started Flower Duet as a part-time weekend business after Casey had finished a career as an officer on board a luxury cruise ship with ports in the Mediterranean and the Caribbean. One of her early jobs on board included designing flowers from around the world. Once Casey settled down in Los Angeles, Kit had immersed herself in floral design courses for a few years, and we started offering flower arranging parties at people's homes. Those parties led to clients who wanted to hire Flower Duet for their weddings, and a new hybrid business was born. We love creating custom wedding flowers, directing corporate team-building reward events for companies like BMW, Mattel, Universal Studios, the NFL, and Fabletics, and teaching flower arranging to budding floral designers and dedicated floral enthusiasts.Flower Duet has been our full-time passion for the last decade. It shows that we are the preferred floral vendors for many area venues, including many numerous luxury venues throughout Los Angeles.In addition to teaching flower arranging classes at our own design studio in the South Bay of Los Angeles, we also teach floral design workshops at The Huntington Library in San Marino and offer tours of the Los Angeles Floral District.Flower Duet is a proud member of the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and of Slow Flowers.Flower Duet has won two awards from the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and been the guest designer for the American Grown Flowers Field to Vase Dinner, Speakers at The Slow Flower Summit in Washington, D.C., presenters at the San Francisco Flower and Garden Show and keynote speakers for dozens of garden clubs around the Southern California area.

The Coleman sisters, Casey Schwartz and Kit Wertz, began their floral design business in 1999.We started Flower Duet as a part-time weekend business after Casey had finished a career as an officer on board a luxury cruise ship with ports in the Mediterranean and the Caribbean. One of her early jobs on board included designing flowers from around the world. Once Casey settled down in Los Angeles, Kit had immersed herself in floral design courses for a few years, and we started offering flower arranging parties at people's homes. Those parties led to clients who wanted to hire Flower Duet for their weddings, and a new hybrid business was born. We love creating custom wedding flowers, directing corporate team-building reward events for companies like BMW, Mattel, Universal Studios, the NFL, and Fabletics, and teaching flower arranging to budding floral designers and dedicated floral enthusiasts.Flower Duet has been our full-time passion for the last decade. It shows that we are the preferred floral vendors for many area venues, including many numerous luxury venues throughout Los Angeles.In addition to teaching flower arranging classes at our own design studio in the South Bay of Los Angeles, we also teach floral design workshops at The Huntington Library in San Marino and offer tours of the Los Angeles Floral District.Flower Duet is a proud member of the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and of Slow Flowers.Flower Duet has won two awards from the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and been the guest designer for the American Grown Flowers Field to Vase Dinner, Speakers at The Slow Flower Summit in Washington, D.C., presenters at the San Francisco Flower and Garden Show and keynote speakers for dozens of garden clubs around the Southern California area.

 What you'll do 

 This Thanksgiving, set a table that’s too pretty to clear. We’ll design a lush autumn centerpiece in a chic rectangular vessel, overflowing with the season’s best blooms. Add in a little styling magic, effortless hosting tips, and a glass (or two) from Divine Vintage—and you’ve got holiday perfection.Difficulty: Beginner Viola Floral Studio: 1639 11th St. Suite 162, Santa Monica Convenient parking in the back of the building.Please note that all workshops are non-refundable, but if something comes up, feel free to send a friend in your place—flower joy is always transferable. Please plan to arrive 15 minutes early to settle in, sip something refreshing, and get ready to bloom.Kit Included Everything is taken care of by our amazing team, including fresh flowers, vases, floral cutters, and guided instructions to create one stunning floral arrangement. Expect to leave with a breathtaking arrangement crafted by your own hands, enriched with newfound knowledge of florals and design. Light bites and bubbly will be provided!Following your purchase, our team will be in touch to coordinate the next steps.

Viola Floral was founded in 2019 by Jelena Trifunovic — floral designer, science educator, and mom of three. Jelena was born and raised in Serbia and moved to Los Angeles at the start of the Yugoslav War in the early 1990s. She studied biology and took her love of science to the classroom — first as a high school teacher and then as a professor at Loyola Marymount University.Jelena grew up arranging flowers with her mother, entertaining and hosting many gatherings both at home and at her family’s restaurant. After her mother passed away from pancreatic cancer in 2016, Jelena decided to pursue her passion for floral design by launching Viola Floral — honoring the bond the two women shared in a meaningful way. Viola Floral began as a labor of love and a path for Jelena to heal, but now (many years and tens of thousands of bouquets later), Jelena leads a team of designers who share her passion for flowers and floral education.

The Coleman sisters, Casey Schwartz and Kit Wertz, began their floral design business in 1999.We started Flower Duet as a part-time weekend business after Casey had finished a career as an officer on board a luxury cruise ship with ports in the Mediterranean and the Caribbean. One of her early jobs on board included designing flowers from around the world. Once Casey settled down in Los Angeles, Kit had immersed herself in floral design courses for a few years, and we started offering flower arranging parties at people's homes. Those parties led to clients who wanted to hire Flower Duet for their weddings, and a new hybrid business was born. We love creating custom wedding flowers, directing corporate team-building reward events for companies like BMW, Mattel, Universal Studios, the NFL, and Fabletics, and teaching flower arranging to budding floral designers and dedicated floral enthusiasts.Flower Duet has been our full-time passion for the last decade. It shows that we are the preferred floral vendors for many area venues, including many numerous luxury venues throughout Los Angeles.In addition to teaching flower arranging classes at our own design studio in the South Bay of Los Angeles, we also teach floral design workshops at The Huntington Library in San Marino and offer tours of the Los Angeles Floral District.Flower Duet is a proud member of the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and of Slow Flowers.Flower Duet has won two awards from the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and been the guest designer for the American Grown Flowers Field to Vase Dinner, Speakers at The Slow Flower Summit in Washington, D.C., presenters at the San Francisco Flower and Garden Show and keynote speakers for dozens of garden clubs around the Southern California area.

The Coleman sisters, Casey Schwartz and Kit Wertz, began their floral design business in 1999.We started Flower Duet as a part-time weekend business after Casey had finished a career as an officer on board a luxury cruise ship with ports in the Mediterranean and the Caribbean. One of her early jobs on board included designing flowers from around the world. Once Casey settled down in Los Angeles, Kit had immersed herself in floral design courses for a few years, and we started offering flower arranging parties at people's homes. Those parties led to clients who wanted to hire Flower Duet for their weddings, and a new hybrid business was born. We love creating custom wedding flowers, directing corporate team-building reward events for companies like BMW, Mattel, Universal Studios, the NFL, and Fabletics, and teaching flower arranging to budding floral designers and dedicated floral enthusiasts.Flower Duet has been our full-time passion for the last decade. It shows that we are the preferred floral vendors for many area venues, including many numerous luxury venues throughout Los Angeles.In addition to teaching flower arranging classes at our own design studio in the South Bay of Los Angeles, we also teach floral design workshops at The Huntington Library in San Marino and offer tours of the Los Angeles Floral District.Flower Duet is a proud member of the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and of Slow Flowers.Flower Duet has won two awards from the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and been the guest designer for the American Grown Flowers Field to Vase Dinner, Speakers at The Slow Flower Summit in Washington, D.C., presenters at the San Francisco Flower and Garden Show and keynote speakers for dozens of garden clubs around the Southern California area.

The Coleman sisters, Casey Schwartz and Kit Wertz, began their floral design business in 1999.We started Flower Duet as a part-time weekend business after Casey had finished a career as an officer on board a luxury cruise ship with ports in the Mediterranean and the Caribbean. One of her early jobs on board included designing flowers from around the world. Once Casey settled down in Los Angeles, Kit had immersed herself in floral design courses for a few years, and we started offering flower arranging parties at people's homes. Those parties led to clients who wanted to hire Flower Duet for their weddings, and a new hybrid business was born. We love creating custom wedding flowers, directing corporate team-building reward events for companies like BMW, Mattel, Universal Studios, the NFL, and Fabletics, and teaching flower arranging to budding floral designers and dedicated floral enthusiasts.Flower Duet has been our full-time passion for the last decade. It shows that we are the preferred floral vendors for many area venues, including many numerous luxury venues throughout Los Angeles.In addition to teaching flower arranging classes at our own design studio in the South Bay of Los Angeles, we also teach floral design workshops at The Huntington Library in San Marino and offer tours of the Los Angeles Floral District.Flower Duet is a proud member of the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and of Slow Flowers.Flower Duet has won two awards from the Torrance Area Chamber of Commerce and been the guest designer for the American Grown Flowers Field to Vase Dinner, Speakers at The Slow Flower Summit in Washington, D.C., presenters at the San Francisco Flower and Garden Show and keynote speakers for dozens of garden clubs around the Southern California area.

Viola Floral was founded in 2019 by Jelena Trifunovic — floral designer, science educator, and mom of three. Jelena was born and raised in Serbia and moved to Los Angeles at the start of the Yugoslav War in the early 1990s. She studied biology and took her love of science to the classroom — first as a high school teacher and then as a professor at Loyola Marymount University.Jelena grew up arranging flowers with her mother, entertaining and hosting many gatherings both at home and at her family’s restaurant. After her mother passed away from pancreatic cancer in 2016, Jelena decided to pursue her passion for floral design by launching Viola Floral — honoring the bond the two women shared in a meaningful way. Viola Floral began as a labor of love and a path for Jelena to heal, but now (many years and tens of thousands of bouquets later), Jelena leads a team of designers who share her passion for flowers and floral education.

Viola Floral was founded in 2019 by Jelena Trifunovic — floral designer, science educator, and mom of three. Jelena was born and raised in Serbia and moved to Los Angeles at the start of the Yugoslav War in the early 1990s. She studied biology and took her love of science to the classroom — first as a high school teacher and then as a professor at Loyola Marymount University.Jelena grew up arranging flowers with her mother, entertaining and hosting many gatherings both at home and at her family’s restaurant. After her mother passed away from pancreatic cancer in 2016, Jelena decided to pursue her passion for floral design by launching Viola Floral — honoring the bond the two women shared in a meaningful way. Viola Floral began as a labor of love and a path for Jelena to heal, but now (many years and tens of thousands of bouquets later), Jelena leads a team of designers who share her passion for flowers and floral education.

## EVENTS

We have a lot of wonderful events at The Farm for all ages between May and November (our seasonal months of operation). Our goal is to provide engaging, family programming where children are always welcome. Some events are free and require no registration, while registration and payment options are available for our Floral Workshops, Maker Mornings and FarmKids (dates below). If you know you would like to attend, we suggest reserving a space as soon as possible. Please click on one of the dates below to reserve and pre-pay a space. Reservations are NOT refundable but you may transfer them to a friend if you discover you are unable to attend.

[6/13 FarmKids: Watercolor Bird of Paradise](https://square.link/u/gZe2qYun)

[6/20 Maker's Morning: Floral Still Life Watercolor Class](https://square.link/u/7gX9rzQY)

[6/27 FarmKids: DIY Fairy Gardens](https://square.link/u/a2QMskoH)

[7/11 Maker's Morning: Watercolor in the Field](https://square.link/u/6kdyHViK)

[7/18 FarmKids: Pollinators](https://square.link/u/G1B4Aifk)

[7/24 FarmKids: Floral Arranging](https://square.link/u/gMkFIVBF)

7/25 Devotions in the Field

[8/1 Floral Workshops: Compote Vase](https://square.link/u/wTMOzoYo)

[8/15 Maker's Morning: Pressed Flowers](https://square.link/u/e3R8T00G)

8/22 Devotions in the Field

8/29 Summer Harvest Festival

[9/4 Line Dancing on the Farm](https://square.link/u/ae1yfjO5)

9/26 Devotions in the Field

10/24 Fall Festival

## Storytime at the Farm

![Image 3: Storytime](https://www.thefarm-salinasvalley.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/BD799E0F-0AD3-473C-A1B9-21FE3517421A-scaled.jpg)

Storytime has been a favorite event with children over the years. Set in our outdoor courtyard, Storytime begins with singing and continues in a fast-paced pattern of three books interspersed with songs. While the average audience age is 0-4 years old, many older children attend and enjoy the stories which are varied, fun and revolve around animal stories and all things farming, with an emphasis on values like kindness, sharing, and working hard.

Wednesdays (through the end of September): 10:00 and 10:30.

No need to register.

## U-Pick Flowers

![Image 4: Jessica flowers](https://www.thefarm-salinasvalley.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Jessica-flowers-scaled.jpeg)

Our self-serve flower field starts the second week of July. It will be open Monday through Saturday 9-4. Come wander through our beautiful field and gather either a hand-held bouquet (22.00) or a 2.5 gallon bucket (42.00). You can bring a bucket of your own to transfer your flowers into after picking or you can package your flowers to go with damp paper towels and plastic bags. All shears, and packaging supplies are provided on our self-serve flower cart at the entrance to the flower field. We recommend wearing close-toed shoes, long sleeves and gloves as some plants we grow can cause skin irritation.

Please pay first at the farmstand counter and check out a pair of shears. Staff will direct you to our field from there!

No need to register.

## Floral Workshops

![Image 5: flower arrangement](https://www.thefarm-salinasvalley.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/IMG_0308-scaled.jpeg)

Our flower arranging workshops are held outdoors in our patio, and focus on using locally grown, seasonally available flowers (most of them sourced from our own farm). We teach the basics of flower arranging without using floral foam. We begin each workshop with a demonstration of technique, and color theory, followed by workshop time for each participant to build their own work of art with opportunity for one-on-one guidance from our farm staff. Each registration also includes a 20% coupon to our Gift Shop, along with complimentary refreshments.

## Maker's Morning

![Image 6: Evening Flowers](https://www.thefarm-salinasvalley.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/IMG_8896-scaled.jpeg)

This series of hands on workshops are designed to create a stress-free environment to create art in a multigenerational setting (children are welcome to attend with their adult, though these workshops are designed for older students).

## FarmKids

![Image 7: Farm school](https://www.thefarm-salinasvalley.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/IMG_8374-scaled.jpeg)

FarmKids are a series of fun, engaging, hands-on classes that cover a variety of farming topics and are designed to engage all ages (toddlers to adults).

Please note that each child or family of children must be accompanied by a parent/guardian.

Viola Floral was founded in 2019 by Jelena Trifunovic — floral designer, science educator, and mom of three. Jelena was born and raised in Serbia and moved to Los Angeles at the start of the Yugoslav War in the early 1990s. She studied biology and took her love of science to the classroom — first as a high school teacher and then as a professor at Loyola Marymount University.Jelena grew up arranging flowers with her mother, entertaining and hosting many gatherings both at home and at her family’s restaurant. After her mother passed away from pancreatic cancer in 2016, Jelena decided to pursue her passion for floral design by launching Viola Floral — honoring the bond the two women shared in a meaningful way. Viola Floral began as a labor of love and a path for Jelena to heal, but now (many years and tens of thousands of bouquets later), Jelena leads a team of designers who share her passion for flowers and floral education.

# Hours and Directions

**May - October**we are open Monday-Saturday, 9AM-5PM.

**November through early May**the store will be closed but the bakery will be going! Go to the office (green house in main parking lot) Monday-Friday, 9AM-4PM (we may be closed during some lunch hours), to pick up pies and other goodies. See the Bakery tab for more info!

The Farm is located in the heart of the Salinas Valley. We’re just a couple miles west of Oldtown Salinas and 15 miles east of Monterey on Highway 68 off the Spreckels Blvd. Exit. If you’re coming down Highway 101, we’re 60 miles south of San Jose and 105 miles south of San Francisco.

## From Salinas and Highway 101

Coming from the north, take Laurel Exit and follow the map above to South Main St and Blanco Rd. intersection. Turn right onto Highway 68 (Monterey-Salinas Highway).  
 Coming from the south, take Sanborn Rd. exit and follow above map to South Main St and Blanco Rd intersection. Turn left onto Highway 68 (Monterey-Salinas Highway).

If you are coming from Salinas, stay on South Main St, which turns into Highway 68.

1.   Continue on Highway 68 out of Salinas.
2.   Take Spreckels Blvd exit.
3.   At the stop sign on the off ramp, turn right onto the farm ranch road. (don’t turn left onto Spreckels Blvd) You will see an art figure of a farmer and a small sign to The Farm. Turn right again. This road will take you to the produce stand.

## From Marina and Highway 1

1.   Take Reservation Rd towards Salinas.
2.   Continue under Highway 68 bridge (Reservation becomes River Rd).
3.   Turn left on to the Highway 68 east on ramp towards Salinas.
4.   Merge onto Highway 68 east.

1.   Take the Spreckels Blvd exit
2.   Turn left on Spreckels Blvd.
3.   At the end of the street, you will see an art figure of a farmer and a small sign to The Farm. At the white fence turn right. This road will take you to the produce stand. Make sure you do not turn right too soon, as this is against traffic coming from Highway 68 going west

Viola Floral was founded in 2019 by Jelena Trifunovic — floral designer, science educator, and mom of three. Jelena was born and raised in Serbia and moved to Los Angeles at the start of the Yugoslav War in the early 1990s. She studied biology and took her love of science to the classroom — first as a high school teacher and then as a professor at Loyola Marymount University.Jelena grew up arranging flowers with her mother, entertaining and hosting many gatherings both at home and at her family’s restaurant. After her mother passed away from pancreatic cancer in 2016, Jelena decided to pursue her passion for floral design by launching Viola Floral — honoring the bond the two women shared in a meaningful way. Viola Floral began as a labor of love and a path for Jelena to heal, but now (many years and tens of thousands of bouquets later), Jelena leads a team of designers who share her passion for flowers and floral education.

 What you'll do 

 As we step into autumn, we notice that nature is ushering us into a new season, and there is a feeling of new possibilities as well as opportunities for growth and reflection. Learn to design a picturesque fall-themed flower arrangement featuring autumn leaves, foliage, and seasonal florals, and learn the tips and tricks of flower arranging like a pro.Everything is taken care of by our amazing team, including fresh flowers, vases, floral cutters, and guided instructions to create one stunning floral arrangement. Expect to leave with a breathtaking arrangement crafted by your own hands, enriched with newfound knowledge of florals and design. Light bites and bubbly will be provided!**Please Note**Following your purchase, our team will be in touch to coordinate the next steps. Please note that all workshops are non-refundable, but if something comes up, feel free to send a friend in your place—flower joy is always transferable. Please plan to arrive 15 minutes early to settle in, sip something refreshing, and get ready to bloom. 

 What you'll get 

 A stunning fall-themed floral arrangement

Viola Floral was founded in 2019 by Jelena Trifunovic — floral designer, science educator, and mom of three. Jelena was born and raised in Serbia and moved to Los Angeles at the start of the Yugoslav War in the early 1990s. She studied biology and took her love of science to the classroom — first as a high school teacher and then as a professor at Loyola Marymount University.Jelena grew up arranging flowers with her mother, entertaining and hosting many gatherings both at home and at her family’s restaurant. After her mother passed away from pancreatic cancer in 2016, Jelena decided to pursue her passion for floral design by launching Viola Floral — honoring the bond the two women shared in a meaningful way. Viola Floral began as a labor of love and a path for Jelena to heal, but now (many years and tens of thousands of bouquets later), Jelena leads a team of designers who share her passion for flowers and floral education.
